title: Parkinson's law
idea: Work expands to fill the time available for it.
apply: Cut the deadline in half on one task this week and see what really gets done.
who: Lena, who has two weeks to write a report.

scenes.sub: It needs about two days of real work.
scenes.nar: Lena gets two weeks to write a report that needs about two days of real work.
With two weeks, the work stretches. She researches again, tweaks the template, waits for inspiration, and writes in a panic on day thirteen.

items: Plenty of time, so no urgency

scenes.nar: So she sets her own deadline of three days. The outline today, the draft tomorrow, a polish on day three.

scenes.sub: The work took as long as she gave it.
scenes.nar: The report goes out on day three. The work took exactly as long as she gave it.
